page0.text:
We should patrol Shinto, where there are more people.
The priest told me to fight if I want to prevent victims.
I'm an untrained mage, so I have no choice but to take Saber with me and call the other Masters out.
...I don't think Kotomine tricked me into it, but I can't think of any other way to go about this than to use myself as bait.

page1.text:
"Let's go to Shinto. If any of the Masters is up to no good, then it'll be easier to deal with them there."
"Understood. Let us head to the other side, then."

page2.text:
I'm well aware that we'll be exposed to danger in Shinto.
...I need to be prepared for the possibility that I might die doing this.
If I'm determined to fight, then I can't make the same mistake that I made with Lancer.

page3.text:
"..."
...I might be new to all this, but I've been trying to teach myself to think like a mage.
I steel myself as we walk, just like I do when I insert the pseudo-nerve of a Magic Circuit into my back.

page4.text:
We spend about an hour patrolling Shinto.
There isn't anything out of the ordinary as far as I can see, and Saber doesn't sense any Servants.

page5.text:
"...Nothing to report in Shinto, then. I thought someone would take the bait if we walked around so defenselessly."
I chastise myself for being so naïve.
Tohsaka might have known a better way to scout out the area.

page6.text:
"No, Master, your actions were correct. If a mistake was made, it was that we failed to account for your skill level.
Nighttime patrols are in no way a waste. Though we may not have encountered anyone tonight, it will lead to results."

page7.text:
"Argh... Well, I hope so."
It hurts, realizing that I'm the one holding us back.

page8.text:
"Let's go back to Miyama. If Shinto didn't work out, then we should check out our home turf."
"Yes. I understand your fervor to seek out our foes, but we should first secure our own territory."

page9.text:
We return to Miyama.
There's no sign of any pedestrians or vehicles on the bridge.
I cross the bridge with Saber in the quiet night.
"!?"
In the next moment,
a terrible chill assails my back, and I hear a scream.

page10.text:
"That came from nearby! What was that, Saber!?"
"I sense a Servant. It appears to be in the park right below us."

page11.text:
"...!"
My heart rate rises.
I knew it.
It's the entire reason we're looking around outside.
But why won't my brain work?

page12.text:
I told myself I was ready to fight.
Any hesitation disappeared the moment I risked my life.
But now, my body won't listen to my brain.

page13.text:
...I'm sick to my stomach at how soft I am.
Whatever conviction I thought I had doesn't manifest.
I went to Shinto to fight, but I was mistaken to think I was prepared for this. I'm not used to fighting and my body isn't responding like I want it to.
That's right.
Going out to do battle and getting attacked means
killing the enemy before they kill me.

page14.text:
...
...I can't move.
I may be used to being attacked, but I'm not used to going on the attack.
I'm such an idiot.
I kept saying I was ready to die, but I never thought about killing anyone else...

page15.text: "Your orders, Master. I don't know what just happened, but the enemy is nearby. If you command it, we can help whoever was just attacked."

page16.text:
...
Maybe it's thanks to Saber's calm voice.
My frozen brain and paralyzed limbs awkwardly start to move again.
The fear of watching someone die drives away
the dread of an imminent battle of life and death.

page17.text:
"I'm sorry, Saber...!"
I break into a dash, apologizing for my own spinelessness,
sprinting towards the source of the scream, and the battle that left such ominous magical energy.
I'm not ready.
My legs are shaking even as I run.
That's the correct response.
If I lack the will to fight, to want the Holy Grail for myself, then that fear will inevitably come for me.
